source: Pagedeck (pagedeck.com/posts), published analyses of DTC landing pages behind long-running paid ads; robots.txt allows reading

rules: Message match: the page's first headline keeps the promise of the ad that sent the visitor.
One goal: the page has one action; every button goes to the same next step.
The offer (price, incentive, what is in it) is visible before the first scroll on a direct-offer page.
Proof sits beside the doubt it answers, never as a block nobody reads.
The buy box does the arithmetic: price against the compare-at, per-unit price, pack, guarantee and shipping terms.
Longevity is the only free signal of a working ad: an ad and page kept live for months are being paid for by results.

formats.built_as: variant B for a cold or lapsed cohort when the brand states three or more reasons; product at item two, a button after each reason, buy box at the end
variant B with two or more pictured products
not built: it needs a problem and mechanism story the brand's record does not state, and carries FTC disclosure duties

note: Figures quoted in those pages (conversion lifts, medians) are Pagedeck's or their sources' and are never printed on a generated page.
